significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that a small set of attention heads preserves an agent-specific stale state after a world update, such that "ablating these heads makes the model default to the true location" while ablation of separate world-tracking heads has the opposite effect. This is a form-(ii) causal decomposition, not merely an existence claim: the proposed dissociation between belief tracking and world tracking fixes an explanation for both false-belief collapse and preserved true-world tracking, a distinction made consequential by controlled-behavior work such as FANToM (Kim et al., 2023) and Clever Hans or Neural Theory of Mind? (Shapira et al., 2024). The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a localized mechanism; verified false would informatively reject the small-dedicated-head account, although it would not by itself discriminate among distributed, shared-circuit, and non-attention alternatives. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on LLM beliefs would not earn this score—the specific predicted double dissociation is what raises it above the topic-median direction-plus-intervention hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is the candidate "false-belief heads," which downstream researchers could use as an ablation or activation-patching target, together with the measurable "belief-world divergence signal." It is principally post hoc: the heads diagnose and causally attribute a false-belief answer after the relevant narrative state has been processed, rather than forecasting failures before stories are attempted or models are deployed. After re-extraction on another model, the claim does not predict a scaling law, threshold, head count, or other transferable relation; it mainly supplies a procedure for looking, and its broader scope is uncertain because it only says it would "test whether the same heads generalize" to non-spatial and second-order beliefs. The topic-substitution check leaves this at the topic median: the head-level double dissociation is claim-specific, but the reusable deliverable remains a model-calibrated interpretability intervention mainly for researchers studying the same mechanism.
